newsitem.title: ESTONIA: PRIVATISATION AGENCY TO SELL 25.06 PCT OF HOTEL.
newsitem.headline: PRIVATISATION AGENCY TO SELL 25.06 PCT OF HOTEL.

text.p: The Estonian privatisation agency said on Wednesday that it had decided to publicly offer 25.06 percent of the shares in the Hotel Olumpia.
"We hope to announce the sale by June," Vaino Sarnet, the agency's director, said at a news conference.
The state currently has a 55 percent stake in the hotel, which is located near the centre of Tallinn.
Sarnet added that the final 30 percent would be sold at a set price of 66 million kroons.
The present shareholders had preemptive rights but waved the right to buy into the public offering.
But they have retained their rights to buy the final 30 percent of the state's stake, Sarnet said.
The hotel had a net profit in 1996 of 20 million kroons.
